Humble expects the company to perform strongly once it moves to production in a few years.

Um, and you may have just seen recently, India announced they're wanting to massively increase their nuclear energy production network. They've got some good contractors down there working on it and they've just had some, um, some, some significant works done in the last few months. So yeah, we think that that's a it's a really good asset they've got down there.

headline: TIP Group's Andrew Coleman notes ASX uranium miners like Deep Yellow face structural challenge getting deposits out of the ground given Australia's mining embargo
reasoning: Coleman observes that the majority of uranium deposits listed on the ASX, including Deep Yellow, Boss Energy and others, are located in Australia where there is effectively a flat-out embargo on uranium mining. While he acknowledges these companies likely have uranium in situ, the key investor question is whether they can ever extract it at a cost and timeframe that makes economic sense. He is broadly supportive of the rational case for uranium and nuclear energy but does not invest in sentiment-driven situations.
quote: Almost all the other Australian uranium plays, is that the majority of their deposits are located in a country that doesn't let you mine them, which is here in Australia. Paladin's of course got some in Africa too, so that gives them at least the ability to make some production and some revenue and profit. But the majority of the uranium mine is that are listed on the ASX, Deep Yellow, boss, etc. even if they've got uranium in situ and I think they do, the question is going to be how are they ever going to get it out at at a cost and in a time frame that makes sense to an investor because at the moment we have a flat out embargo, basically on on mining it.
